This guide continues the official collection “Linear Algebra I — Weeks 1–4” and cov-
ers weeks 5−7of the fall semester 2026. It collects every question and every formula
from each course file and the assigned textbook sections — each problem with a com-
plete step-by-step solution, as in the main collection.
Course files covered (weeks 5–7): lectures; practical sessions and in-class problems
with solutions; Independent Study Assignments (ISA); the expanded week 5 Beamer
theory notes; EXTRA material (week 6 review with examples). Textbooks: G. Strang,
Introduction to Linear Algebra (4thed.), with the parallel companion Linear Algebra
and Its Applications (4thed.).
How each week is organised. First comes the formula catalog: all definitions, theo-
rems and rules of the week with explanations. Then, for every source file, a “ques-
tions and complete solutions” section: in-class problems, the practical session, In-
dependent Study Assignments (ISA) and extra material. Problems are reproduced
verbatim; solutions are complete, step by step, with checks.

Exercise 47. Advanced problem. Prove that Null(AT A) = Null(A)for any real
matrix A.
Solution. Two inclusions. (1)IfAx = 0, then AT Ax = AT (Ax) = 0, that is, Null(A) ⊆

sum of squares of the coordinates of Ax is zero, which means Ax = 0. Conclusion:
Null(AT A) = Null(A); a consequence is that AandAT A have the same null space and
rank (least squares fact).
